prompt.brief: Design a predictive-maintenance platform that ingests equipment telemetry, detects anomalies, estimates remaining useful life, and creates actionable maintenance work before failures occur.
successSignals: Separate raw timestamped telemetry, equipment and sensor metadata, feature windows, model predictions, alerts, and work orders.
Use event-time windows and equipment partitions, handle missing or out-of-order readings, and preserve the evidence behind a prediction.
Turn predictions into deduplicated maintenance recommendations with operator acknowledgement and feedback loops.
Explain cold-start equipment, sensor drift, false alarms, safety escalation, offline operation, retention, and model rollback.

functional: Register equipment and sensors, ingest telemetry, calculate features, score failure risk and remaining life, and create work recommendations.
Expose equipment health, anomaly evidence, prediction confidence, model version, sensor freshness, and maintenance status.
Support acknowledgements, overrides, corrective labels, reprocessing, access control, audit history, and model evaluation.
nonFunctional: Target above 90% recall for critical failures at a declared false-alarm budget and keep health dashboards below 2 seconds p95.
Ingest 1 million sensor readings per second by equipment and site partitions without losing safety-critical alerts.
Make telemetry ingestion, feature windows, predictions, alerts, and work-order creation idempotent.
Fall back to threshold rules and last-known health when model workers or upstream telemetry are degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Monitor 1 million assets, 100 million sensors, and 1 million readings per second across sites with intermittent connectivity.
Partition by tenant, site, asset, sensor, and event time; isolate high-rate assets and incident bursts.
Retain raw telemetry, feature definitions, predictions, labels, alerts, and work-order decisions under safety policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Predictive-maintenance platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Predictive-maintenance platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Predictive-maintenance platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Predictive-maintenance platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Predictive-maintenance platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Predictive-maintenance platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Predictive-maintenance platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Predictive-maintenance platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Predictive-maintenance platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
